_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-09 · SkyDesk — the MAP team now has one page showing what is waiting on them, and it counts everything fresh each time you open it instead of trusting a written list.
_status: There is a new tab, MAP Team Queue, that answers one question: what is waiting on us, and how long has it been waiting. It is the inward-facing twin of the college page we are about to build. The reason it re-counts everything each time you open it is worth knowing, because it changed the plan: the written backlog we inherited was two days old and already wrong in two places. It said nobody had been named as an owner on the Governance page — the team had in fact named all seventeen on the 5th and 7th. It said six pieces of Sierra feedback were waiting; there are twenty-three, the oldest sitting since 1 July. And the contact work was smaller than advertised in one direction and bigger in another: only fourteen colleges are actually waiting on a decision from the MAP team, because forty-two of the fifty-six already have a contact in MAP — but seven colleges that cannot route a student request had never been looked up at all, because the original search only covered colleges without a CPL Assistant, and having one does not mean MAP knows where to send a student. Those seven are the cheapest thing on this list: one web lookup each. Separately, the Sierra feedback queue was 61% our own automated test writing into it; that is fixed at the source now, so what you see there is real people. Next up is the college-facing half — the page a college opens to find out what it should do next — and the one thing blocking its most important section is a single view name from Malone.

items.text: Seven colleges have nowhere for a student CPL request to land and have never been looked up: Citrus, College of the Canyons, Palomar, Saddleback, Yuba, plus Futuro Health and Launch Apprenticeship. One web lookup each — the cheapest real work we have.
Twenty-three pieces of real feedback on Sierra are waiting to be read, nine of them thumbs-down. The oldest has been sitting since 1 July. The robot rows that used to drown this list are gone.

Fourteen colleges have no contact in MAP and we have a suggested one for each. Send them to the MAP team to accept or reject. (Not 56 — the other 42 already have a contact in MAP, so there is nothing to decide there.)

Send Malone the Custom Report request (docs/map_custom_report_request_for_malone.md). One view name unblocks the nightly refresh, which the college page needs before it can promise anyone today's to-dos.
Four colleges publish no usable address at all for a credit question. These need a human to make a call, not another search.
The college contact-refresh cadence was decided in June and still has not run once. Owners are all assigned now, so this is the one governance item with nothing behind it.
Confirm the Year-2 metrics for the three $35M priorities are final. The college page reads them live, so changing them there changes the page.
Build the college-facing briefing on the same engine as the queue — a college picks itself and a role and gets a rendered briefing, never a blank chat box.
Seed the to-do library from the IFM P1/P2/P3 strategies rather than inventing advice. Knowing a college's state is not the same as knowing what moves it.
